subject: crab
pitch: A feisty red rock crab with one oversized claw raised in challenge. A wide, knobbly shell in brick red speckled with orange and cream, eyes on stalks, eight jointed walking legs with pointed tips, and claws with dark tips and little teeth on the pinchers. A tiny barnacle and a strand of seaweed cling to the back of its shell.
reasoning:
I'm planning the crab's proportions and skeleton structure, sizing the shell around 0.3m wide with legs positioned along the sides and a root body joint to build the rig from.

For the shell itself, I'm using a scaled sphere with mottled brick-red and cream speckle paint plus a lighter countershaded belly, and adding small knobby spheres scattered across the shell's surface using randomized spherical coordinates.

Now I'm planning the finer anatomy: front rim teeth as small cones, eye stalks as tilted cylinder-and-sphere joints near the front, a dark box for mouthparts, and the legs as four-point polyline chains per side running from hip to knee to ankle to foot, mimicking the classic crab leg bend with coxa, merus, carpus, and propodus segments.

Still naming leg joints and wiring up capsules...

For the final segment I'll use a pointed spike shape for the claw tip, with distinct coloring: reddish body, lighter orange joints, and dark tips. Now I'm planning the arm chain's shoulder and elbow positions to raise a large claw on the right side.

For the claw fingers, I'm planning a fixed spike-shaped finger from the palm base to tip and a movable one hinged at a "clawJawL" joint so they can open slightly apart, with the hand oriented upward-forward for the raised challenge pose.

Still shaping claw details...

Now I'm setting up the bone joints for the fixed hand and jaw, then working out the arm skeleton chain — shoulder, elbow, and wrist points leading to a named hand joint at the path's end.

Scaling fingers up for an oversized claw look, then planning the smaller right claw with its own shoulder-to-hand chain and jaw joint, mirrored but angled differently so it points forward-in rather than up-forward. I'm sketching out a reusable claw-building function parameterized by side so I can handle the differing opening-axis directions for left versus right.

Now thinking through the mouth: a dark front box under the eyes plus a separate jaw joint with a small mandible box, attached below the upper lip piece on the root, keeping everything positioned relative to the shell's front edge.

I'm now working out shell geometry, checking the ellipsoid dimensions and hip joint positions for the legs so each leg attaches correctly at the shell's edge for both front and back leg rows.

Continuing to plot crab leg points, defining hip, knee, elbow, wrist, and tip coordinates with an outward z-offset so each leg arches up then down, and setting decreasing segment radii from hip to tip for a tapered look.

I'm naming the five joints per leg (coxa, merus, carpus, propodus, dactyl) and chaining them into a polyline-based bone structure with the tip as the spike segment, plus adding a small orange sphere marker at the knee joint and starting to place eye stalk joints.

Now I'm positioning the eye stalks with capsule geometry and dark spherical eyes with small white highlights, computing where each stalk's tip sits along its direction vector, and solving for the shell's curved surface height at the eye-socket location using the ellipsoid equation.

I'm scattering small bumpy knobs across the shell's ellipsoid surface using polar coordinates, computing their positions while avoiding the eye zone, and varying their size and color slightly for a natural textured look.

Now I'm adding rim teeth cones along the front edge of the shell between -60° and 60°, angling them outward and forward, and considering whether to darken the paint near the rim for extra depth.

For the shell texture, I'm layering a reddish mottle base with orange-and-cream spots, cream near the belly, using paint/spots/mottle SDK functions, and applying similar speckled coloring to the legs. I'm also starting a cluster of cone barnacles on the back of the shell.

Adding barnacle positioning and seaweed strands...

I'll switch to using catmull-rom smoothing for the strand paths and add small green bladder bulbs along the seaweed. Then I'm checking joint counts stay under budget and sizing the crab so the raised claw and shell proportions look proportionate but dramatically oversized.

Now I'm writing the claw builder function, chaining shoulder/elbow/wrist/hand joints into tapered capsule segments with slightly larger spheres at the joints, and positioning the palm relative to the shell.

Working out finger placement...

Adding teeth cones for each tooth position with cream-colored cones and dark spike tips, positioning them along the inward direction with offset radii based on jaw position.

Now I'm writing the leg generation loop, building each leg chain with named segments (coxa, merus, carpus, propodus, dactyl) parented to root, then setting up the root joint at the body center.

I'm also fleshing out the shell parts, adding a darker rim layer and underside shading using scaled sphere geometries for a layered carapace look.

For the eyes, I'm placing black and white highlight spheres at the tips of the eye stalks, computing stalk direction and offset positions so they sit naturally forward-facing. I'm also defining a surface height function for the seaweed base so it follows the shell's curvature, then wrapping up the build.
